subject: Information Theory
title: Approaching the Limit
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Approaching the Limit.

hook.text: Shannon proved the entropy floor in 1948. It took 60 years of coding theory to get within touching distance.

buildup.text: Huffman codes came in 1952. Arithmetic coding in the 1970s. Each generation crept closer to the limit.

discovery.text: ANS (asymmetric numeral systems) by Jarek Duda in 2009 matches arithmetic coding's compression at Huffman's speed.

twist.text: For channel coding, LDPC and turbo codes reached within fractions of a decibel of Shannon's limit.

climax.text: The gap between theory and practice is now razor-thin. Shannon's bounds have gone from dreams to engineering specs.

punchline.text: Sixty years from theory to practice. Almost there.

quiz.question: What did ANS achieve in compression?
options: Matched arithmetic coding's efficiency at Huffman's speed
